milestone.title: mp autopilot CLI rename — pivot `mp watch` to `mp autopilot` with legacy alias

intent.outcome: Users invoke `mp autopilot [start|status|stop|output|result|config|session]` instead of `mp watch`; `mp watch` continues to work as a deprecated alias that issues a notice pointing at the new command.

problem.description: `mp watch` is overloaded — it is simultaneously the verb ("watch this milestone be driven"), the surface verb in the raul Watch lane (M198), and the noun for the watched agent (M149). The new autopilot system replaces the 2-pane runner+coordinator model with a 3-pane orchestrator+runner+reviewer architecture, so the verb changes meaning. We need a single top-level command (`mp autopilot`) that owns start, status, stop, output, result, config, and session verbs; the old `mp watch` alias is kept for one release with a deprecation notice (F2), then removed.

in_scope: Introduce `mp autopilot [start|status|stop|output|result|config|session|<args>...]` as the primary command tree, delegating to the same internal implementation that powers today's `mp watch`.
Add `mp watch` as a thin alias that prints a deprecation notice on stderr (F2 will move the notice into a non-blocking warning; this milestone just keeps the alias functional).

Update internal references from `watch` to `autopilot` in the cargo workspace (folder names stay `crates/mp/src/watch/` for the first pass; a later follow-on can rename, but renaming is out of scope here to keep this milestone small and reversible).
Update integration tests that referenced `mp watch` directly to call `mp autopilot` (legacy alias is tested separately under F2).
out_of_scope: Removing the `mp watch` alias — that's F2.
Renaming the source folder `crates/mp/src/watch/` to `crates/mp/src/autopilot/` — kept as `watch/` until the rest of the autopilot system stabilizes; a follow-on track can do the rename later.
Renaming the raul `Lane::Watch` to `Lane::Autopilot` — that's D1.
Updating the consumer surface (skills, docs, templates) — that's F3.

acceptance_criteria.description: `mp autopilot --help` lists the autopilot verb tree (start, status, stop, output, result, config, session) with descriptions matching today's `mp watch` and `mp watch-control` sub-commands.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p mp --test autopilot_cli_tree --no-fail-fast exit 0 (11/11 pass)

acceptance_criteria.description: `mp watch` and `mp autopilot` accept the same arguments and return identical exit codes and stdout bytes; the only permitted difference is the single legacy deprecation line on `mp watch` stderr.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p mp --test watch_alias_equivalence --no-fail-fast exit 0 (10/10 pass)

acceptance_criteria.description: A versioned legacy watch-state fixture migrates once into the M207 session schema; status/list/show preserve session identity, queue order, pane IDs, and lifecycle state. Re-running migration is idempotent.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p mp --test autopilot_legacy_state_migration --no-fail-fast exit 0 (13/13 pass)

acceptance_criteria.description: Unknown, corrupt, or partially migrated legacy state fails with a typed diagnostic and leaves both the legacy source and any existing autopilot session unchanged.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p mp --test autopilot_legacy_state_migration --no-fail-fast exit 0 (13/13 pass)

acceptance_criteria.description: `mp session` planning workflows and `mp autopilot session` drive workflows have unambiguous CLI nesting, help text, storage paths, and diagnostics; neither command can read or mutate the other session domain.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p mp --test watch_cli --no-fail-fast exit 0 (15/15 pass)

design_decisions.choice: `mp autopilot <verb>` is a top-level clap subcommand tree; `mp autopilot session <verb>` is a nested subcommand for session bookkeeping.
design_decisions.rationale: Single root keeps the namespace flat; session becomes a first-class entity per the A1 schema, so its verbs cluster under one branch.

design_decisions.choice: `mp watch` is implemented as a clap-level alias (clap supports `alias = "watch"` on the autopilot command) so both names walk the same code path.
design_decisions.rationale: Avoids divergent behavior; the alias lives or dies with the clap definition, and F2's removal is a one-line change.

design_decisions.choice: Migration is explicit, versioned, idempotent, and rollback-safe; the legacy file is retained until the new session validates and is atomically committed.
design_decisions.rationale: The herdr test exposed truncation and stale-binary regressions. A best-effort shared backend is insufficient for durable compatibility.

findings.description: autopilot_help_stop_replaces_watch_control_stop test passes for incidental reasons: help.find("stop") returns the index of the first occurrence which is inside the status verb description ("Replaces `mp watch-control status`\n  stop …"), so the snippet already contains "watch" before reaching the stop verb line. The stop verb's own description says "gracefully stop the recorded autopilot run by signaling its PID" and does not contain "watch" or "control". The AC-01 spec ("matching today's mp watch and mp watch-control sub-commands") is satisfied semantically — the autopilot stop description matches watch-control stop ("gracefully stop the recorded live watch …") with watch → autopilot. But the test would pass even if the stop verb description omitted the migration pointer entirely. Backlog: tighten the test to scope to the stop verb's own line.
findings.author: reviewer-208

findings.description: crates/mp/src/commands/autopilot.rs lines 437-457 ship three #[allow(dead_code)] reserved-for-future items that pull in three otherwise-unused imports at lines 30-31: _AUTOPILOT_TOPOLOGY (uses AutopilotTopology), _ac_surface (uses AcStatus, ProjectionKey, ProjectionWriteOutcome), _emit (no new imports, just wraps the existing emit()). The dead-import stubs pattern matches M211 F-01 (low/style, task_assign.rs lines 600-620). Clippy is silenced via the allow attribute, so the lint is benign today, but the surface ships intentional dead code with explicit "reserved for future" comments that future contributors can leave untouched. Backlog: remove the stubs and the associated imports when no follow-on milestone lands in scope.
findings.author: reviewer-208
